summary: The paper demonstrates that enriched native two-qubit control via the AshN scheme—combining tunable coupling with simultaneous microwave drives—enables SWAP absorption into adjacent gates, effectively increasing the connectivity of superconducting qubit processors with fixed coupling graphs. On benchmark circuits with 1D and 2D topologies, AshN compilation achieves 45.2% and 43.7% reductions in two-qubit gate count compared to controlled-Z, with experimental validation on an 8-qubit Dicke state achieving 0.736 fidelity and certified genuine multipartite entanglement even under connectivity defects.
motivation: Planar superconducting processors face routing bottlenecks due to sparse connectivity, requiring extra SWAP gates to implement distant interactions. This work addresses whether richer native gate sets can mitigate connectivity constraints without adding physical couplers, by exploiting closure properties under SWAP composition.
method: The authors calibrated AshN gates across a 12-qubit 1D chain and 3×3 2D array using parallel calibration procedures that exploit characteristic Hamiltonian dynamics, implemented SWAP-aware MirrorSABRE routing to absorb SWAP operations into adjacent two-qubit blocks, and benchmarked the resulting circuits against controlled-Z implementations on seven circuits, larger compilation instances, and Dicke-state preparation under connectivity defects.
result: For structured application circuits, two-qubit gate count overhead relative to all-to-all connectivity decreased from 1.65× (CZ) to 1.13× (AshN) on 2D lattices, and the 8-qubit Dicke state fidelity improved from 0.631±0.001 (CZ) to 0.736±0.001 (AshN), with the AshN implementation certifying genuine multipartite entanglement across defective topologies where CZ-based implementations failed.
